AGENDA
  GLENDALE WATER AND POWER COMMISSION
  (STAFF ACCESS ONLY) GLENDALE WATER AND POWER DEPARTMENT
  633 E. Broadway, Room 105 (MSB 105)
  Glendale, CA 91206
 Welcome to the meeting of the Glendale Water and Power Commission. Meetings are broadcast
 live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for
 program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office.
 Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at
 https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal. If you have any question about
 matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the Glendale Water and Power
 Administration Office at (818) 548-2107 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.
 In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
 language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
 are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
 requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
 to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
 are public records, will be available for review in the Glendale Water and Power Administration Office,
 141 N. Glendale Ave., Suite 450, Glendale, CA 91206.
 Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
 wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
 Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
 the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
 required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  JULY 6, 2020 AT 4:00 PM

Due to the evolving situation with the COVID-19 novel coronavirus and health recommendations from
the LA County Health Department, the Glendale Water and Power Commission meeting will be
available to the public electronically.

Due to social distancing requirements, the public will not be able to attend the meeting. The public is
encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes to practice social distancing.

The meeting can be viewed:
On local cable: Charter Cable Channel 6 and AT&T U-verse Channel 99.
Streaming Online: https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal

  1
 For public comments and questions during the meeting call (818) 937-8100.

City staff will be submitting these questions and comments in real time to the appropriate person
during the Glendale Water and Power Commission meeting.

1.  ROLL CALL – 4:00 PM
2.  CONSENT ITEMS – (INCLUDING MINUTES)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the
  Commission or the audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such
  request before motion is proposed.
  a. Approval of the March 02, 2020 Meeting Minutes
3.  GWP COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
4.  REPORTS - INFORMATION
  a. PFAS Chemical Monitoring in the City of Glendale’s Water Supply
  b. Low Carbon Fuel Standard Program
  c. GWP Cares Program
5.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS (5) Minutes
  Discussion is limited to items NOT part of this agenda. Each speaker is allowed five (5)
  minutes – Commission may question or respond to the speaker, but there will be no debate or
  decision. The General Manager may refer the matter to appropriate staff for investigation and
  report.
6.  AGENDA FORECAST
  a. Agenda Forecast 07/06/2020
7.  ADJOURNMENT

MINUTES
  GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION

  MUNICIPAL SERVICES BUILDING
  633 E. Broadway, 1st Floor, Room 105 - Glendale, CA 91206

  Monday, July 6, 2020, 4:00 PM

1. ROLL CALL
  The meeting was called to order at 4:05 p.m.

  Present: President Kedikian, Commissioners Avanessian, Flanigan, Jazmadarian, and Lall

2. CONSENT ITEMS
  a. Approval of the March 2, 2020 Meeting Minutes
  The Commission approved the minutes as published.

3. GWP COMMISSION/ STAFF COMMENTS
  Mr. Michael De Ghetto, Chief Assistant General Manager of GWP, welcomed new
  Commissioners Ted Flanigan and Nina Jazmadarian. Commissioners Flanigan and
  Jazmadarian stated that they look forward to serving on the GWP Commission. Mr. De
  Ghetto informed the Commission that the Water Department’s Consumer Confidence Report
  is available on the GWP website under the “About Your Water” tab. He also warned the
  public to be aware of scam callers seeking payment for overdue utilities.

  Atineh Haroutunian, Public Benefits Marketing Manager for GWP, notified the Commission
  that GWP had received two awards from the American Public Power Authority: 1) an award
  for GWP’s “D.E.V.O.T.E.” program, through which GWP employees volunteer in the
  community, and 2) a “Smart Energy Provider” Award. The Commissioners congratulated
  GWP on the APPA awards. President Kedikian and Commissioners Avanssian and Lall
  welcomed the new commissioners.

4. REPORTS – INFORMATION
  a. PFAS Chemical Monitoring in the City of Glendale’s Water Supply. Mr. De Ghetto
  described the PFAS chemicals (Perfluoroalkyl and Polyfluoroalkyl, known as PFOS and
  PFOAS), where they are found (i.e., Teflon, dental floss, carpeting, fire treatment
  applications), and how they are regulated (by the federal Environmental Protection Agency
  and by the State Water Resources Control Board). Mr. De Ghetto described the water
  treatment in place at the Glendale Operable Unit, located near the Grayson Power Plant,
  and operated under a federal Consent Decree, which also removes PFAS from the water.
  Mr. De Ghetto provided the test results of the PFAS that was done at the State Water
  Resource Control Board's request, as well as additional testing, which is voluntarily
  undertaken by GWP. He stated that the test results show that PFAS is not detected in
  most wells. In a few of the south wells that form part of the Glendale Operable Unit, some
  PFAS were detected, but the levels drop down to "non-detect" after treatment and before
  water is served to customers.
  1
   Mr. De Ghetto stated that GWP continues to work with the Department of Drinking Water
  to monitor PFAS and emphasized that GWP is focused on maintaining safe and reliable
  water service in Glendale, including rigorous and frequent water quality testing. In
  response to Commissioner questions, Mr. De Ghetto explained that the Glendale
  Operable Unit is funded by the Glendale Respondent's Group, at no cost to the City as it
  operates under a consent decree. He stated that the GS-1 well shows the highest
  concentrations because it is designed to capture the contaminant "plume" as part of the
  consent decree remedy.

  b. Low Carbon Fuel Standard Program. Mr. Craig Kuennen, Deputy General Manager –
  Business Services, presented the Low Carbon Fuel Standard program. GWP receives
  “Low Carbon Fuel Standard” credits, which can be monetized and used to fund and
  promote electrification of vehicles in the Glendale Water & Power service territory and will
  be used for the statewide point of sale electric vehicle rebate program. Mr. Kuennen
  stated that GWP currently holds approximately 28,000 Low Carbon Fuel Standard credits,
  which are valued at roughly $5.5 Million based upon recent transactions. Mr. Kuennen
  noted that by participating in the Clean Fuel Rewards Program, GWP expects to continue
  to receive approximately 12,000 credits per year. Mr. Kuennen responded to
  Commissioner questions. He confirmed that the credits are utilized to fund EV programs
  and point-of-sale rebates in Glendale Water & Power’s service territory. Commissioner
  Flanigan inquired whether GWP receives credits through its CNG busses; Mr. Kuennen
  stated that he would find out. Mr. Kuennen noted that Glendale would be signing a
  contract to join the point-of-sale program, which will be managed initially by the Southern
  California Edison on behalf of all state participants.

  c. GWP Cares Program. Mr. Kuennen described the Glendale Cares Program, a new
  temporary bill relief program, to help mitigate the economic impact of COVID-19 on
  electric residential and business customers. The program provides eligible customers with
  a one-time bill credit of $150 for single-family and business customers, $80 for residential
  customers in multi-family housing, and $60 for Glendale Senior Care and Glendale/ Care
  program. The enrollment period is from July 1 to October 31, 2020. GWP expects 25,000
  applicants and has budgeted $3 Million for the program.

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  None.

6. AGENDA FORECAST
  President Kedikian stated that he would be unavailable for the August Commission meeting.
  Commissioner Lall agreed to serve as President Pro Tem. The Commissioners reviewed and
  approved the agenda for the August 2020 meeting with the following changes:

  GWP Commissioner Elections (Secretary) moved to October 2020 meeting.
  Annual Consumer Confident Report –eliminated as a duplicate agenda item.
  Urban Water Management Plan (UWMP)– eliminated as it was included in error; it is not
  currently the UWMP reporting period.

  Commissioner Lall requested an informal update regarding the effect of COVID-19 on GWP’s
  system.

  Commissioner Flanigan requested an update regarding the Clean Power Plan. Ms. Godinez
  stated that work on the plan is underway, and she would defer to Mr. Zurn on the timing;
  Commissioner Flannigan requested the report as soon as possible.
  2
 7. ADJOURNMENT
  Motion to Adjourn:
  Moved by: Commissioner Avanessian
  Seconded by: Commissioner Lall
  Motion Passed.
  The meeting was adjourned at 5:15 pm
